answer_text:
# 🤰 How to Read Pregnancy Test Results

Here is a complete guide to understanding your pregnancy test results:

---

## 🔬 How Pregnancy Tests Work

Pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants in the uterine lining. Once this happens, the placenta forms and produces a hormone called **human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)** — and it's this hormone that a home pregnancy test detects to tell you if you're pregnant.

hCG levels are initially very low but **double approximately every 48 to 72 hours** in early pregnancy.

---

## ✅ Positive Result

A pregnancy test is **positive** when **two lines** appear — one in the Control (C) region and one in the Test (T) region. Even if the second line is faint, it still indicates the presence of the hCG hormone, confirming pregnancy.

- **Digital tests** are the easiest to read — the result window will clearly say **"Pregnant"** or **"Yes"** if you're pregnant.
- **Single-window tests** will show two lines side-by-side if positive — one is the control line and the second is the result line. **Two-window tests** will show a line in the smaller control window and a **"+"** sign in the larger window.

---

## ❌ Negative Result

A **negative result** means only **one color band** appears on the top Control (C) region, with no apparent band on the Test (T) region.

- A digital test will say **"Not Pregnant"** or **"No"** if you're not pregnant.
- **False-negative results are more common than false-positive results.** If your test is negative but you still don't get your period in two days, take another test.

---

## ⚠️ Invalid Result

If there is **no visible control line**, the test is invalid — discard the test and repeat with a new device.

If no line appears, or there's only one line in the (T) region but not the (C) region, or the test window is blurry or unreadable, the test is **invalid**.

---

## 🔍 Faint Line — What Does It Mean?

A faint line is, **in the vast majority of cases, a positive line**. It indicates that hCG is present, but the concentration in your urine may still be relatively low — this is typical in very early pregnancy.

The line may be faint because you tested early, your urine was diluted, or you naturally have lower initial hCG levels. If you see a faint line, you should **consider yourself pregnant** and confirm with another test in a few days.

---

## ⏱️ Evaporation Lines — Don't Be Fooled

An **evaporation line** is a faint, colorless streak that can appear in the test window **after the urine has dried and the designated reading time has passed**. It is **not** a positive result — it is a residue left by evaporated urine.

Distinguishing faint lines from evaporation lines comes down to **timing and color**. A faint (positive) line will appear within the recommended window (usually 3–5 minutes) and will activate the dye, appearing blue or light pink.

---

## 🕐 When to Read the Test

You'll want to read your test **between 5 and 10 minutes** after taking it. Beyond that window, you may see an evaporation line, which isn't the same as a positive.

---

## 📅 When to Take the Test

Many modern tests advertise their ability to detect pregnancy several days before a missed period. While this is possible, **accuracy is significantly higher after your period is due.**

For the most accurate result, use your **first-morning urine**. This sample is typically more concentrated and contains the highest level of hCG if you are pregnant.

---

## ⚕️ Next Steps

A home pregnancy test is a **screening tool** and should not be used as the only basis for diagnosis. Your healthcare provider should confirm pregnancy based on a full clinical evaluation.

> **Always consult your doctor** for confirmation and next steps, whether your result is positive or negative!
